title: E-commerce order with exactly one line item
rationale: Identical in shape to the passing fixture, differing only in element count. Array inference requires a parsed size strictly greater than 1, so a one-item order - the modal case in most order systems - takes a completely different and wrong path. The highest-frequency real-world defect in the family.
catchesBugClass: Cardinality-dependent structural inference: the same schema round-trips differently depending on how many rows the array happens to hold. Also catches the absence of any schema or arity sidecar in the wire format.
cannotCatch: It does not distinguish the two independent faults it triggers - the size>1 gate and the dead raw-vs-encoded lookup. If someone fixes only the gate, this goes green while the lookup stays dead.

predicted.detail: The array becomes an object AND its leaves become JSON text: both the container type and the leaf types are wrong.
